newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close mixed, hoteliers recover. [CORRECTED 19:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close mixed, hoteliers recover. [CORRECTED 19:36 GMT]

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Tuesday, with a mild recovery among tourist firms, and traders predicted a short stabilisation period before possible further growth for some popular issues.
"Most tourist firms recovered after a slump in the past weeks, and I expect them to establish themselves at the present level through the week", said Zoran Ilic from Consult Invest brokerage.

Of five Istrian hoteliers four were up from last week. The biggest gainer Laguna added 50 kuna ($9.38) to close at 1,300, Arena closed 30 kuna up at 170, Jadranturist gained 15 to come at respectable 285 kuna, and Riviera rose 20 kuna to 170.
Ilic said the market showed signs of recovery after government assurances that investors who had bought shares on the secondary market would not be hit by some unresolved ownership issues.
"The trading is slowly picking up again, although the volume is still very small," he said.
Of 15 active issues, seven were up, four down, three remained flat and one was traded for the first time. Turnover was up at 3.8 from 2.1 million kuna, volume also higher at 6,772 from 4,842 shares.
The biggest loser was Zagrebacka Banka 2C-series issue which fell 100 kuna to close at 500, with 11 shares sold. The bank's other preferential issue, 3E-series rose 30 kuna to close at 450.
Most actively traded issue was food producer Podravka which sold 2,084 shares at 229 kuna, six up from Friday.

Drug firm Pliva traded flat at 13,500 kuna on volume of 153 shares, and Zagrebacka Banka lost 4 kuna to close at 995, with 403 shares traded. Both are expected to remain stable at this price within an eight percent margin.
Electric manufacturer Koncar, listed for the first time on the Zagreb bourse on Monday, was traded at 380 kuna -- 20 percent of its nominal value.
(Corrects the dollar-kuna exchange rate and adds the currency name)
